financials_interim.notes: Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026), same filing (p.5,7,9), COMPANY (standalone holding-company) basis. Company has no cost of sales (gross_profit=revenue, a pure holding/management company); operating_profit = 'Profit from operating activities' (8,174,624). Company PBT fell 83% YoY (17,808,001 to 2,948,860) and PAT fell 94% (15,417,736 to 972,750) despite Group-level PBT/PAT both growing strongly -- the Company (parent-only) result is dominated by 'Other Income' (up 104% to 4,767,498, but off a small base) and a swing in Net Finance Income/(Cost) from -2,107,185 to -5,225,764 (finance cost roughly flat but finance income fell 64% to 1,726,545 from 4,834,585), i.e. the parent earned much less on its own cash/investments this quarter than a year earlier, unrelated to the e-commerce operating business consolidated only at Group level. Identity check ties: PBT-tax=PAT (2,948,860-1,976,110=972,750); total_assets=total_liab+total_equity (1,600,921,947=322,904,738+1,278,017,209). cash_and_equivalents = balance-sheet line (7,114,972), net of Rs.47,247 overdraft per Note 11 = 7,067,725 (matches cash flow closing balance). short_term_borrowings = current Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings (46,249,004) + Bank Overdraft (47,247) = 46,296,251. long_term_borrowings = non-current Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings (88,415,883). capex = Acquisition of PPE (1,833,184).

Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026), p.5 balance sheet, p.6 income statement, p.9 cash flow. GROUP basis. Figures in the filing are in whole Rs (not Rs'000), hence unit_scale='1'. operating_profit = 'Profit/(Loss) from operating activities' (5,071,019), which already nets 'Other Income and Gains' (19,779,228); this is the filing's own subtotal before Finance Cost/Income. Identity checks tie exactly: PBT-tax=PAT (24,906,293-5,724,038=19,182,255); total_assets=total_liab+total_equity (1,461,949,219=605,702,764+856,246,455, where total_liabilities=Non-Current Liab 268,907,762 + Current Liab 336,795,002). DATA-QUALITY FLAG: the filing's own EPS note (8.6, p.12-13) computes 'Earning/(deficit) per share' by dividing 'Net profit/(loss) for the period' -- but the figure it plugs in for Group 2026 is 16,852,790, which is actually TOTAL COMPREHENSIVE INCOME (profit 19,182,255 plus OCI of -2,329,465 FX translation loss), not the profit-for-the-period figure (19,182,255) shown two lines above it in the same note and in the P&L itself. 16,852,790/164,130,360=0.1027, rounding to the printed 0.10 -- confirming this is how the filing derived its own headline EPS. The correctly-computed PAT-based EPS would be 19,182,255/164,130,360=0.1168 (~0.12). eps_basic is stored here as the filing's own printed/disclosed figure (0.10) for consistency with the source document, with this discrepancy flagged for the record. (For Company basis this quirk is invisible because Company had zero OCI, so PAT and TCI coincide.) cash_and_equivalents = balance-sheet 'Cash & Cash Equivalents' line (128,751,028); Note 11 shows this net of a Rs.515,627 bank overdraft = 128,235,401, which is what the cash flow statement's own 'Cash and Cash Equivalents at the end of the quarter' reconciles to. short_term_borrowings = current 'Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings' (101,273,282) + Bank Overdraft (515,627) = 101,788,909 (combined, as there is no separate dedicated 'short-term borrowings' line distinct from these two). long_term_borrowings = non-current 'Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings' (117,750,546) only. capex = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant and Equipment' (48,127,845), stored as a negative outflow; note the Group also had a large PPE disposal (sale proceeds 90,819,131) this quarter, which is why 'Net Cash Flows from Investing Activities' is a large net INFLOW (85,073,761) despite the capex outflow. shares_in_issue = 164,130,360 (Note 8.4, unchanged during the period).

thesis.thesis_text: Kapruka Holdings PLC is an e-commerce/holding company whose Group Revenue grew 20.0% YoY to Rs.537,902k in Q1 FY2026/27, with Group PBT and PAT both swinging from losses a year earlier to profits (PBT: Rs.(1,619)k to Rs.24,906k; PAT: Rs.(5,569)k to Rs.19,182k). The swing is concentrated below the operating line: Net Finance Income improved Rs.19,126k YoY (~72% of the total PBT improvement) and an undisclosed 365% surge in Other Income and Gains contributed further, while both Administrative and Selling & Distribution Expenses grew faster than revenue. A data-quality flag in the filing's own EPS Note 8.6 (apparently dividing Total Comprehensive Income rather than Profit for the Period) means the printed Rs.0.10 EPS likely understates the correct PAT-based figure (~Rs.0.12). At ~39-47x annualised P/E and ~3.6x P/B, the stock is priced for a durable turnaround that the current quarter's earnings composition does not yet support, and the standalone parent company's results moved in the opposite direction entirely (PBT -83.4%, PAT -93.7%) on a fall in its own finance income (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id 52619, p.6 and Note 8.6 p.9).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no e-commerce/consumer-sector data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend), sector is unclassified in coverage_universe, no dividend/shareholder data exists, and a specific EPS-computation discrepancy in the filing's own Note 8.6 (Total Comprehensive Income vs Profit for the Period) further caps confidence in the headline per-share figures.

financial_quality.rationale: Group PBT swung from a Rs.1,619k loss to a Rs.24,906k profit YoY, and PAT swung from a Rs.5,569k loss to a Rs.19,182k profit, but the swing is concentrated below the operating line: Net Finance Income alone improved Rs.19,126k YoY (Finance Income +204% to Rs.27,061k), accounting for roughly 72% of the total Rs.26,525k PBT improvement, and Other Income and Gains surged 365% to Rs.19,779k with its composition undisclosed. Both major operating cost lines -- Administrative Expenses (+35.9% to Rs.148,483k) and Selling & Distribution Expenses (+26.8% to Rs.86,880k) -- grew faster than the 20.0% revenue increase. A genuine data-quality flag exists in the filing itself: Note 8.6's printed Group EPS of Rs.0.10 appears to divide Total Comprehensive Income (Rs.16,853k, which includes a Rs.2,329k FX-translation OCI loss) rather than Profit for the Period (Rs.19,182k) -- correctly PAT-based EPS would be closer to Rs.0.12. At the standalone Company level, results moved in the OPPOSITE direction: PBT fell 83.4% and PAT fell 93.7% YoY, driven by a 64.3% fall in the parent's own Finance Income -- a result unrelated to the Group-level e-commerce turnaround.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue grew 20.0% YoY to Rs.537,902k (2025: Rs.448,519k), a genuine top-line improvement for the e-commerce/holding business, and Gross Profit grew faster still (+28.9% to Rs.220,654k, margin expanding to 41.0% from 38.2%). However, no segment-level detail is disclosed in this filing, so the drivers of revenue growth (new customer acquisition vs average order value vs new product lines) cannot be identified beyond the single consolidated line. The swing to an operating and pretax profit is driven more by non-operating items (finance income, undisclosed other income) than by operating leverage on the revenue growth, tempering how much of this trajectory is likely to repeat mechanically.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.18.80 (2026-08-28), annualising the filing's own printed Q1 EPS of Rs.0.10 (x4 = Rs.0.40) implies a P/E of ~47x; even using the arguably more correct PAT-based EPS of ~Rs.0.12 (x4 = Rs.0.48), P/E is still ~39x. Book value of ~Rs.5.22/share (total equity Rs.856,246k / 164,130,360 shares) implies a P/B of ~3.60x. Both multiples are rich for a company whose swing to profitability this quarter was driven predominantly by non-operating finance income and an undisclosed surge in other income rather than operating-leverage improvement. No dividend data is on file.

business_quality.rationale: Kapruka Holdings is an e-commerce/holding company (sector not classified in coverage_universe) with a genuine 20.0% revenue growth rate this quarter -- a positive consumer-facing growth signal. However, the standalone parent (Company) results deteriorated sharply and in the opposite direction to Group (PBT -83.4%, PAT -93.7%), driven by a fall in the parent's own investment/finance income, unrelated to the e-commerce operating business only consolidated at Group level -- a structural complexity investors need to separate carefully. The lack of segment disclosure limits how well the underlying e-commerce business quality can be assessed independent of holding-company-level effects.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists to verify board or ownership changes. A specific, quantifiable disclosure-accuracy concern is present in the filing itself: the printed Group EPS (Rs.0.10, Note 8.6) appears to be computed from Total Comprehensive Income rather than Profit for the Period, understating what a PAT-based calculation would show (~Rs.0.12) -- this is stored/used as-disclosed for fidelity to the source, but the underlying computational error is itself a mild governance/disclosure-quality flag. The composition of a 365%-growth Other Income line is also undisclosed.

key_reasons: Group PBT/PAT swung from losses to profits YoY (PBT: Rs.(1,619)k to Rs.24,906k; PAT: Rs.(5,569)k to Rs.19,182k) on 20.0% revenue growth, but the swing is concentrated in non-operating items: Net Finance Income improved Rs.19,126k YoY, ~72% of the total PBT improvement

Valuation is rich (~39-47x annualised P/E depending on which EPS figure is used, ~3.60x P/B) for a profit swing driven predominantly by finance income and an undisclosed 365% surge in Other Income rather than operating leverage

Standalone Company (parent) results moved in the OPPOSITE direction to Group -- PBT -83.4%, PAT -93.7% YoY -- driven by a 64.3% fall in the parent's own Finance Income, unrelated to the e-commerce operating turnaround
watch_factors: The filing's own printed Group EPS of Rs.0.10 (Note 8.6) appears to be computed from Total Comprehensive Income rather than Profit for the Period -- a PAT-based calculation would show closer to Rs.0.12, worth confirming in the next filing
Composition of the 365%-growth Other Income and Gains line (Rs.19,779k) is undisclosed -- a meaningful contributor to the operating-profit swing that cannot be verified as recurring

Both major operating cost lines (Administrative +35.9%, Selling & Distribution +26.8%) grew faster than the 20.0% revenue increase -- underlying operating leverage has not yet materialised despite the topline growth

horizon_notes.6m: Next quarterly filing will clarify whether the 20.0% revenue growth continues and whether operating costs finally grow slower than revenue, or whether profitability continues to depend on non-operating income.
horizon_notes.1y: If Net Finance Income and Other Income normalise without repeating, Group PBT/PAT could revert toward the small-loss levels seen a year ago -- worth confirming against a full-year trend.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether the e-commerce operating business can generate genuine operating leverage; no segment data yet exists in this project to test that independent of holding-company effects.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess Sri Lanka e-commerce/consumer-spending trends relevant to Kapruka's multi-year trajectory.

interim_updates.note_text: Kapruka Holdings PLC (KPHL) reported a swing from a Group PBT LOSS of Rs.1.619mn in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Group PBT PROFIT of Rs.24.906mn in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), and Group PAT swung from a Rs.5.569mn LOSS to a Rs.19.182mn PROFIT, on Group Revenue growth of 20.0% YoY to Rs.537.90mn (2025: Rs.448.52mn). Group Profit/(Loss) from operating activities swung from a Rs.2.328mn LOSS to a Rs.5.071mn PROFIT (the filing's own printed 'Change' column shows 318%, reflecting a swing across zero rather than a conventional percentage growth). The single largest driver below the operating line is Net Finance Income, which swung to Rs.19.835mn INCOME from just Rs.0.709mn a year earlier (+2,698% per the filing's own computation) -- Finance Income alone rose 204% to Rs.27.061mn (2025: Rs.8.910mn), which is the dominant contributor to the PBT swing from loss to profit (Rs.26.525mn total PBT improvement, of which the Rs.19.126mn improvement in Net Finance Income accounts for roughly 72%). Gross Profit rose 28.9% YoY to Rs.220.65mn on 20% revenue growth (margin expanded to 41.0% from 38.2%), while Administrative Expenses rose 35.9% to Rs.148.48mn and Selling & Distribution Expenses rose 26.8% to Rs.86.88mn -- both cost lines grew faster than revenue, meaning the swing to an operating profit was driven more by 'Other Income and Gains' surging 365% to Rs.19.779mn (2025: Rs.4.254mn) than by underlying operating leverage; the composition of this Other Income line is not broken out in the interim filing (gap). Income Tax Expense rose 44.9% YoY to Rs.5.724mn (2025: Rs.3.950mn) despite the swing from a pretax loss to a pretax profit, consistent with the much larger taxable profit base. Group Basic/Diluted EPS is printed as Rs.0.10 (2025: Rs.(0.03)) but carries a DATA-QUALITY FLAG identified in this DB's financial_statements notes: the filing's own EPS Note 8.6 appears to divide Total Comprehensive Income (Rs.16.853mn, which includes a Rs.2.329mn FX translation OCI loss) rather than Profit for the Period (Rs.19.182mn) by the 164,130,360 share count -- 16,852,790 / 164,130,360 = 0.1027, rounding to the printed 0.10, whereas PAT-based EPS would correctly be 19,182,255/164,130,360 = 0.1168 (~0.12); the filing's own printed 0.10 figure is what is stored here for consistency with the source document. At Company (standalone parent, e-commerce/holding operations) level the picture is the OPPOSITE of Group: Company Revenue fell 7.1% YoY to Rs.52.538mn (2025: Rs.56.579mn) and Company PBT fell 83.4% to Rs.2.949mn from Rs.17.808mn, PAT fell 93.7% to Rs.0.973mn from Rs.15.418mn -- driven by Company Finance Income falling 64.3% to Rs.1.727mn (2025: Rs.4.835mn) while Finance Cost was roughly flat (Rs.6.952mn vs Rs.6.942mn), swinging Company Net Finance Income/(Cost) to a Rs.5.226mn COST from a Rs.2.107mn COST (a Rs.3.119mn unfavourable move), i.e. the parent earned materially less on its own cash/investment book this quarter, a result unrelated to and opposite in direction from the e-commerce operating business that is only consolidated at Group level.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is KPHL's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (Q1 is the first quarter of KPHL's FYE-March fiscal year; only the filing's own YoY comparator column is used). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the composition of Group 'Other Income and Gains' (Rs.19.779mn, +365% YoY) is not broken out by source -- this is a meaningful contributor to the swing to an operating profit but cannot be further decomposed from the document; (2) the filing's own printed Group Basic/Diluted EPS of Rs.0.10 (Note 8.6) appears to be computed off Total Comprehensive Income rather than Profit for the Period -- flagged as a data-quality issue in the underlying financial_statements notes, and the filing's own (arguably mis-derived) figure is what is stored/used here rather than a recalculated one, to stay faithful to the source; (3) no segment-level detail is disclosed in this filing (no segmental note), so the drivers of the 20% Group revenue growth (new customer acquisition vs. average order value vs. new product lines) cannot be identified beyond the single consolidated revenue line; (4) Company-level Finance Income's 64.3% YoY fall is not explained (what investment/deposit balances moved) -- a genuine gap given its outsized effect on Company PBT/PAT.
interim_updates.takeaway: KPHL's Group-level swing from loss to profit is real but is concentrated below the operating line -- Net Finance Income (+Rs.19.13mn YoY, driven by a 204% jump in Finance Income) and an undisclosed 365% surge in Other Income and Gains together explain most of the Rs.26.5mn PBT improvement, while both major operating cost lines (Administrative, Selling & Distribution) grew faster than the 20% revenue increase. The printed Group EPS of Rs.0.10 likely understates true per-share profitability given the apparent Total-Comprehensive-Income-based computation in the filing's own Note 8.6 (PAT-based EPS would be closer to Rs.0.12). Most strikingly, Company (parent, standalone) results moved in the opposite direction entirely -- PBT down 83.4% and PAT down 93.7% YoY -- driven by a 64.3% fall in the parent's own Finance Income, a result investors should not conflate with the Group-level e-commerce operating business, which is only consolidated at Group level.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.537.90mn, +20.0% YoY (2025: Rs.448.52mn); Group PBT swung to a Rs.24.906mn PROFIT from a Rs.1.619mn LOSS; Group PAT swung to a Rs.19.182mn PROFIT from a Rs.5.569mn LOSS.
Net Finance Income swung to Rs.19.835mn INCOME from Rs.0.709mn PY (Finance Income +204% to Rs.27.061mn) -- accounts for roughly 72% of the total Rs.26.525mn Group PBT improvement.

Other Income and Gains (Group) rose 365% YoY to Rs.19.779mn (2025: Rs.4.254mn), composition not disclosed; Administrative Expenses +35.9% to Rs.148.48mn and Selling & Distribution Expenses +26.8% to Rs.86.88mn both grew faster than the 20% revenue increase.

Group EPS printed as Rs.0.10 (2025: Rs.(0.03)) but the filing's own Note 8.6 computation appears to use Total Comprehensive Income (Rs.16.853mn) rather than Profit for the Period (Rs.19.182mn) as the numerator -- correctly PAT-based EPS would be closer to Rs.0.12.

Company (parent) results moved in the OPPOSITE direction to Group: Revenue -7.1% YoY to Rs.52.538mn, PBT -83.4% to Rs.2.949mn, PAT -93.7% to Rs.0.973mn, driven by Company Finance Income falling 64.3% to Rs.1.727mn (2025: Rs.4.835mn).
key_drivers: Net Finance Income swing (Rs.0.709mn to Rs.19.835mn, driven by Finance Income +204% to Rs.27.061mn) is the single largest driver of the Group PBT swing from a Rs.1.619mn loss to a Rs.24.906mn profit.

Other Income and Gains surging 365% to Rs.19.779mn (composition undisclosed) is a second material contributor to the swing to an operating profit, offsetting Administrative and Selling & Distribution Expenses both growing faster than the 20% revenue increase.

Company-level Finance Income falling 64.3% YoY to Rs.1.727mn is the specific driver of the Company PBT decline (-83.4%), a result opposite in direction to and unrelated to the Group-level operating turnaround.

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
